{{tl|PD-Egypt-stamp}} |Berne date = {{TrDate|1977-6-7}} |WTO date = {{TrDate|1995-6-30}} |WIPO treaty = |URAA date = {{TrDate|1996-1-1}} }} This page provides an overview of '''copyright rules of Egypt''' relevant to uploading works into Wikimedia Commons. Note that any work originating in {{wp-Egypt|Egypt}} must be in the public domain, or available under a free license, in both Egypt and the United States before it can be uploaded to Wikimedia Commons. If there is any doubt about the copyright status of a work from Egypt, refer to the relevant laws for clarification. ==Background== The British took effective control of Egypt in the late 19th century, and on 5 November 1914 it became a British protectorate. Britain unilaterally declared that Egypt was independent on 22 February 1922, but retained a military presence until 1954. Egypt has been a member of the {{wp-Berne Convention|Berne Convention}} since 7 June 1977 and the {{wp-World Trade Organization|World Trade Organization}} since 30 June 1995. As of 2018 the {{wp-World Intellectual Property Organization|World Intellectual Property Organization}} (WIPO), an agency of the United Nations, listed ''Law No. 82 of 2002 on the Protection of Intellectual Property Rights'' as the main IP law enacted by the legislature of Egypt. WIPO holds the text of this law in their {{wp-WIPO Lex|WIPO Lex}} database. A copy of the English text is also held on Commons. ''Law No. 82 of 2002'' repealed Law #354 of 1954, and repealed any provisions of that law that contradicted the provisions of the new law.{{sref|82/2002 Article 2(c)}} The 1954 law, in turn, was ''retroactive'' in terms of application to the already-existing works: "The provisions of this law shall apply to all works existing at the time of its entry into force. However, with regard to calculating the duration of protection for existing works, the period that elapsed from the date of the event specified for the commencement of the period up to the date of entry into force of this law shall be included in calculating this period."{{sref|354/1954 Article 50}} ==General rules== According to ''Law No. 82 of 2002'', *The author's economic rights are protected throughout the lifetime of the author and for 50 years from the date of his death.{{sref|82/2002 Article 160}} *The economic rights relating to works of joint authorship are protected throughout the lives of all co-authors and for 50 years from the death of the last survivor.{{sref|82/2002 Article 161}} *For collective works, other than works of applied art, **Where the copyright holder is a legal entity, the economic rights are protected for 50 years from the date on which the work was published or made available to the public for the first time, whichever comes first.{{sref|82/2002 Article 162}} **Where the copyright holder is a natural person, the protection period is calculated as in Articles 160 and 161.{{sref|82/2002 Article 162}} *The economic rights relating to a posthumous work expire after 50 years from the date the work was published or made available to the public for the first time, whichever comes first.{{sref|82/2002 Article 162}} *The economic rights relating to a work published anonymously or under pseudonym are protected for 50 years from the date the work was published or made available to the public for the first time, whichever comes first.{{sref|82/2002 Article 163}} *The economic rights of the author of a work of applied art expire 25 years from the date on which the work was published or made available to the public for the first time, whichever comes first.{{sref|82/2002 Article 164}} *Producers of sound recordings enjoy an exclusive economic right for 50 years from the date on which the recording was made or made public, whichever comes first.{{sref|82/2002 Article 167}} ==United States status== As a result of the {{wp-Uruguay Round Agreements Act|Uruguay Round Agreements Act}}, *For non-creative photographic or audiovisual works copyright has expired in Egypt if published prior to 1987 and copyright has expired in the U.S. if published prior to 1981. *For other works with an identifiable author, copyright has expired in Egypt if the author died prior to {{ #expr: {{CURRENTYEAR}} - 50 }} and copyright has expired in the U.S. if the author died prior to 1946 or published prior to {{max|1923|{{#expr:{{CURRENTYEAR}}-95}}}}. *For other works that are either anonymous or pseudonymous, copyright has expired in Egypt if published prior to {{ #expr: {{CURRENTYEAR}} - 50 }} and copyright has expired in the U.S. if published prior to 1946 *For other works (e.g. collective works) whose copyright is held by a legal person, copyright has expired in Egypt if published prior to {{ #expr: {{CURRENTYEAR}} - 50 }} and copyright has expired in the U.S. if published prior to 1946. ==National folklore== {{Comseealso|Commons:Paying public domain}} National folklore is any expression which consists of distinctive elements reflecting the traditional popular heritage, which originated or developed in Egypt, including in particular:{{sref|82/2002 Article 138(7)}} *Oral expressions such as folk tales, poetry and charades, and other folklore; *Musical expressions such as popular songs accompanied by music; *Motion expressions, such as popular dances, plays, artistic forms and rituals; *Tangible expressions such as: Products of popular plastic art, particularly drawings with lines and colours, engravings, sculpture, ceramics, pottery, woodwork and any inlaid designs, mosaics, metal or jewellery, hand-woven bags, needlework, textiles, carpets and clothes; Musical instruments; Architectural forms. National folklore shall be considered part of the public domain of the people. The competent ministry shall exercise the author's economic and moral rights and shall protect and support such folklore.{{sref|82/2002 Article 142}} ==Copyright tags== {{CRT shortcut|TAG|Egypt}} *{{tl|PD Egypt}} – for all works other than those listed below. *{{tl|PD-Egypt-folklore}} – for works deemed part of Egypt's national folklore. *{{tl|PD-Egypt-official}} – for official documents. *{{tl|PD-Egypt-stamp}} – for Egyptian stamps published prior to 1946. ==Currency== {{CRT shortcut|CUR|Egypt}} {{OkMark}} According to ''Law No. 82 of 2002 on the Protection of Intellectual Property Rights'': "[Copyright protection] shall not cover the following: Official documents, whatever their source or target language, such as laws, regulations, resolutions and decisions, international conventions, court decisions, award of arbitrators and decisions of administrative committees having judicial competence."{{sref|82/2002 Article 141}} ==Freedom of panorama== {{CRT shortcut|FOP|Egypt}} {{NotMark}}, personal use only permitted (interpretation based on Article 171(2) structure). According to Article 171 of Law No. 82 of 2002: *Without prejudice to the moral rights of the author, pursuant to the provisions of the law herein, the author may not prevent third parties, after the publication of his work, from undertaking any of the following acts: ...{{sref|82/2002 Article 171}} *Make a single copy of the work for one's exclusive personal use, provided that such a copy shall not hamper the normal exploitation of the work nor cause undue prejudice to the legitimate interests of the author or copyright holders; :However, the author or his successor may, after the publication of the work, prevent third parties from carrying out any of the following acts without his authorization: * Reproduction or copying works of fine, applied or plastic arts, unless they were displayed in a public place, or works of architecture; ...{{sref|82/2002 Article 171(2)}} The placement of the "unless they were displayed in a public place" clause inside Article 171(2) indicates that it may be part of the personal-use limitation, rather than an independent freedom of panorama. This would mean that reproductions of public art or architecture are lawful only for personal use and not for publication, redistribution, or commercial purposes. While the text appears textually broad, covering {{wp-Applied art|applied art}} and fine arts (such as painting, photography, and sculpture) as well as architecture, there is no known Egyptian case law or authoritative legal commentary supporting a broader interpretation that would allow commercial use. Because Commons requires that works be freely reusable for any purpose, including commercially, Egypt is treated here as a country without valid freedom of panorama. Past acceptance of Egyptian FOP on Commons has been based on a broader reading of the law without supporting case law. Discussion/s: [[Commons:Village pump/Copyright/Archive/2025/08#Egyptian FoP|August 2025]]. === In the repealed laws === There was no FOP-related clause among the Articles 11–17 of the repealed ''Law No. 354 of 1954 on the Protection of Copyright''. The closest provision, Article 17, stated: "In textbooks and in books on literature, history, science, and the arts, it is permissible to quote previously published works in graphic arts, three-dimensional art, or photography, provided that the quote is limited to what is necessary to clarify the text. In all cases, the sources quoted and the names of the authors must be clearly cited." Note: all Egyptian art and architecture made before 1954 are subject to copyright protection, through the retroactive clause under Article 50, though the calculation of duration is based on "the period that elapsed from the date of the event specified for the commencement of the period up to the date of entry into force of this [1954] law". The 2002-20 law retained the 50-year general term of protection. {{See also|Category:Egyptian FOP cases}} ==Stamps== {{Comseealso|Commons:Stamps/Public domain}} {{NotMark}}: [[w:Egypt Post|Egypt Post]], which issues Egyptian stamps, is very assertive of its rights. The website as of 2011 said that "all materials in this site including photos, software and databases, texts, graphics, signs, general appearance and other contents are protected by intellectual property rights of Egypt Post and the copyright stipulated in the Egyptian laws and international treaties."https://web.archive.org/web/20110125094105/http://www.egyptpost.org/en/sitePage.asp?pid=9, and as of 2024, Egypt Post has a copyright notice on its website. https://web.archive.org/web/20240430202453/https://egyptpost.gov.eg/ar-eg/home/# Use {{tlx|PD-Egypt-stamp}} for stamps published before 1946. ==See also== *{{pg|Egypt}} *[[:Category:License tags of Egypt]] ==Citations== {{reflist|refs= {{cite web|url=http://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/results.jsp?countries=EG&cat_id=11 |accessdate=2018-11-04 |title=Egypt Copyright and Related Rights (Neighboring Rights)|year=2018|publisher=WIPO: World Intellectual Property Organization}} {{cite web|url=http://www.wipo.int/edocs/lexdocs/laws/en/eg/eg001en.pdf |accessdate=2018-11-04 |title=Law No. 82 of 2002 on the Protection of Intellectual Property Rights |year=2002 |publisher=Egypt}} [[:File:Egyptian Intellectual Property Law 82 of 2002 (English).pdf|Law No. 82 of 2002 Pertaining to the Protection of Intellectual Property Rights]] }} {{Commons:CRT disclaimer}} {{translatable template|CRT list2}} [[Category:Commons licensing help by country{{#translation:}}|Egypt]] [[Category:Copyright law of Egypt]] [[Category:Paying public domain{{#translation:}}|Egypt]]
